description:
La Torre del Visco stands in the Matarraña region, in southern Teruel, one of Spain's best-preserved rural areas, often ranked among the country's most beautiful and least crowded corners. The hotel is a member of Relais & Châteaux, the prestigious international association of independent historic and gastronomic hotels and restaurants, certifying both the authenticity of the building and the quality of its culinary offering — Mediterranean, local, and European cuisine, drawn from the property's own kitchen garden.

Today its rooms — Junior Suites, Suites, and Superior Double Rooms (28-35 sqm) — sit within the restored fortified farmhouse, with views over the garden and mountains.

The property's Relais & Châteaux membership ties La Torre del Visco to the same mark of international prestige carried by other high-end properties already featured in this collection.

The estate's own kitchen garden, directly supplying its restaurant, gives La Torre del Visco a genuinely farm-to-table culinary identity distinct from properties with a purely decorative agricultural theme.

The castle's position within the Matarraña, a region prized for its relative lack of mass tourism, gives guests staying at La Torre del Visco access to an unusually undisturbed rural corner of Spain.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** In Fuentespalda, Province of Teruel, Aragon, in the Matarraña region.

**Rooms & rates:** Junior Suites, Suites, and Superior Double Rooms (28-35 sqm), with garden and mountain views; from €350 per night, breakfast available for a supplement.

**On-site:** Seasonal outdoor pool, garden, own kitchen garden, library, free bicycles, shared kitchen, concierge and tour organization, restaurant serving Mediterranean, local, and European cuisine.

**Good to know:** A Relais & Châteaux member — the same mark of international prestige carried by other high-end properties in this collection; a strong gastronomic angle with its own kitchen garden and tasting menu.

**Combine with:** The wider Matarraña region, one of Spain's most undisturbed rural corners.
